data.turoyo: (Pfarrer:) huleli kurəsyo mqabəl diḏe. Ono w hiye yatiwina, i foṯo bi foṯo, w b foṯo gaḥaxto fəgʕo šafiro stəqbal, šafiro maqbeleli.

data.turoyo: Omər: "Bir defa gavursun yetmez mi?" — b gaḥxo yaʕni — "Lə bas yo, d kətat gawər, gədhowət naqla ḥreto gawər?"

summary: New sense 1: zum Lachen bringen
rationale: The m-prefixed magḥaxwayli at 51/21 contrasts causative laughter with causing distress. The nominal tegḥixo in a fable-purpose comment is grouped with the same causative, not a second meaning.

summary: New sense 2: (mit ʕal) täuschen, zum Narren halten
rationale: At Jan 2.12/2991 the ʕal-target is the recipient of bogus written charms (mxarxəṭiwonne palləkat); layt ... dugle explicitly denies their efficacy. This supports deceiving, beyond observable laughter or ridicule. One passage with two tokens; not two independent attestations.

data.turoyo: Haṯe latyo šrolo, ăma čirók̇eyo. (Afrem: Hawxa daḥ+ḥănak̇e, du+tegḥixo). E. Hayo šróloyo, haṯe lo.

data.turoyo: ʕAl u gaḥxo w ʕal i raḥmuṯo kogoḥax w komagḥəx.

summary: The existing lachen sense already includes mocking ʕal targets. The present data show affectionate/social laughter, ridicule and ordinary laughter; no sense split is justified by the translation alone.

ʕal marks a stimulus or target, including a person or an interrogative. b foṯe describes laughing toward someone’s face and has both warm (106/28) and teasing (88/19) settings. It does not independently establish a new government sense or a fixed idiom.
I Infectum-wa has both habitual (59/89) and unrealized/reproachful (JTM 4.2/13) readings. German narrative past forms in PrS do not turn the Turoyo Infectum into Preterit.

Stem III is supported directly by magḥaxwayli, not inferred solely from an English causative translation. The alleged Preterit base is not supplied and is not invented. tegḥixo remains a machine-proposed nominal/Infinitiv classification.
The x/k filing split is inherited and cross-referenced. This patch leaves gḥx and gḥk intact; a verb appearing inside another root’s example does not mean it already has its own form box.
gaḥaxto is an attributive feminine form in b foṯo gaḥaxto. Its Part act. treatment is proposed provisionally; a lexical adjective analysis remains possible.

Repeated parenthetical gaḥxo/Gaḥxo is invariant across male and female speaker headings, including Jan 3.52/1478 (Jan alone). It cannot establish feminine Preterit agreement or plural Infectum. It is provisionally filed as Infinitiv on the independent nominal evidence b gaḥxo (Jan 2.4/654), laǧan gaḥxo (Jan 2.12/2995), and the checked gḥk Infinitiv gaḥko. No bare annotation is added as a paradigm example.

Jan includes oral interviews and editorial stage directions as well as written prose. Finite gaḥəx/gaḥəxina/gaḥixi contrast with ko-/k- Infectum and -wa habitual forms. gəḥxi at Jan 2.10/2400 sits in a coordinated habitual Infectum sequence; its contracted form remains ambiguous and is not added.

The existing Preterit Intransitive and Infectum cells each reached five in round 1. Further routine Jan tokens do not fill a gap. The new deception construction is kept distinct from ordinary mockery at Jan 1.28/1326, where claims about magic alone do not entail successful deception.
ʕal u gaḥxo and bu gaḥxo at Jan 3.17/341 are nominal manner expressions. No lexicalized light-verb idiom is demonstrated. Preserve the inherited gḥx/gḥk cross-reference.
Jan English is the project machine translation, not an edition translation. It is reproduced only as supplied and is not evidence for senses; all semantic decisions rest on the Turoyo.
III base-form coverage is updated: round 1’s magḥax is retained from magḥaxwayli, while Jan komagḥəx attests the unextended Infectum variant magḥəx. The Preterit remains unattested.
Confirm tegḥixo as the III Infinitiv, rather than an independent noun; provide III Preterit and an independently attested unextended Infectum base.
Confirm Part act. status and the feminine paradigm of gaḥaxto at 68/22.
Check Gaxiḥi at PrS 42/74 against the edition; metathesis or transcription error could not be determined.
Confirm the gəḥxət / gaḥixət Infectum–Preterit contrast at PrS 19/37.
At 24/251 does aʕli attach to the reporting frame “you said about me”, or to the quoted laughter predicate?
Should the inherited gḥx / gḥk variant entries eventually be consolidated? No duplicate-entry correction is applied here because their editorial treatment is unresolved.
Confirm the nominal Infinitiv treatment of invariant parenthetical gaḥxo rather than a transcript-specific nonfinite annotation; no recording was available within the permitted inputs.
Confirm whether gəḥxi at Jan 2.10/2400 is contracted Infectum within habitual speech or a Preterit Intransitive switch.
Does gəḥxiwo ʕal at Jan 2.12/2991 lexicalize deception, as the sham-charms context suggests, or retain a mocking meaning? The proposed construction is marked for editorial review.

summary: A whole town as feminine collective subject alternates with plural inhabitants; this is participant agreement, not a new laughter sense.
ko-magḥəx supports round 1 zum Lachen bringen and gives an unextended finite Infectum; no second proposal of that sense.
